menuNote: High Nose, sur la Mürrenfluh, au-dessus de la vallée
operator: No drop zone: a BASE site. Landing cards and the rules: Swiss BASE Association; jump clearance from Air-Glaciers (BaseApp).

aerodrome.name: Lauterbrunnen valley, BASE landing field below the Mürrenfluh

fineRelief.why: The terrain tiles round the Mürrenfluh off over a hundred metres: the cliff needs the national survey, sampled every 6 m.

origin.what: middle of the meadow taken as the landing field, on the valley floor east of the Stechelberg road

landingAreas.name: Meadow on the valley floor below High Nose

target.evidence: No target on a BASE landing field: the middle of the meadow is where one aims.

base.name: High Nose
base.evidence: Swiss BASE Association exit table (Lauterbrunnen guide PDF): High Nose, rock drop 7 s / 190 m, altitude to landing 585 m, on the Mürrenfluh. Its exact position is not published: this one is the nose of the Mürrenfluh found in swissALTI3D at 46.57908, 7.90510 (edge, 1355 m): a wooded top sloping gently to the edge, a 190 m drop (1349 m to 1160 m within 6 m), then the face and the scree down to the valley floor at 810 m, 545 m below. The run starts 25 m back from the edge, heading 120 (ESE), straight at the meadow 470 m away.

wind.description: INFERRED: the valley wind blows up the valley, from the north, on summer afternoons; mornings are calm, which is when most jump.

invented: Exit position: High Nose's coordinates are not published; the nose used here matches its published rock drop (190 m) and nearly its altitude to landing (545 m against 585 m).
Landing field: the official landing fields are given out with the landing card; this meadow on the valley floor in line with the exit stands in for them.
Pattern and wind: inferred from the shape of the valley.
